messages:
sarah: Heads-up — we've had a few customer reports where signed upload URLs (S3-style presigned PUTs) fail intermittently. Looks like our gateway is normalizing paths and stripping duplicate query keys before the auth service verifies the signature. 403s for otherwise-valid clients.

kevin: Ugh. Is the gateway deduping qs params like `X-Amz-Date`/`X-Amz-Signature`? That would definitely bork the sig.

mai: Quick dump of the failing example:
```
PUT /uploads/abc/..//file.txt?X-Amz-Credential=...&X-Amz-Date=20260201T120000Z&X-Amz-Signature=abcd1234 HTTP/1.1
Host: uploads.redwood.example
```
Client signs the original URL; our path canonicalizer collapses `..//` to `/` and our query dedupe normalizes order, so the string-to-sign differs.

eli: Two orthogonal problems: (1) path canonicalization must be either exact-same for signing and verification, or skipped for signed routes; (2) header injection (we add `x-client-id` for quota routing) must not mutate the canonical request used by signature verification.

kevin: Agreed. Proposal: add a new config flag on routes `preserve_signed_canonical` that tells the gateway to bypass normalization and query reordering for auth step. Then downstream observability can still see a normalized path for routing/caching after verification.

mai: That sounds reasonable. Implementation detail: we need a two-phase pipeline: 1) compute canonical-string from raw incoming bytes (no reorders, no injected headers) and call auth; 2) if auth passes, run our existing rewrite passes (collapse duplicate qs, add headers for quotas, normalize path) for routing/caching.

infra-bot: Deploy note: gateway config change will require canary on a subset of edge boxes; we should ensure per-route flag defaults to `false` and opt-in for customer-facing upload routes.

sarah: Also: quota routing currently uses `x-client-id` header injected by the gateway before we hit auth. If we postpone header injection until after auth, quota service won't see client id in traces for auth failures. We want traces for failed auth too.

eli: Two ways: (A) inject `x-client-id` only for telemetry (non-canonical) but keep a separate internal header `x-client-id-raw` that is never included in canonical string — i.e., mark it as non-signing metadata; or (B) auth service itself extracts client id from credentials and returns it in the auth response so gateway can re-inject safely.

kevin: I prefer B for long term (single source of truth), but it's more invasive. A can be faster: we add an annotation to header injection middleware to mark headers excluded from canonicalization. Less risky for short rollout.

mai: If we go with annotation approach, update docs and ensure our canonicalizer ignores headers with `x-rw-noncanonical: true` metadata. Also add an integration test: generate presigned URL, send with weird path segments + duplicate qs and assert gateway accepts when route has `preserve_signed_canonical: true`.

sarah: Good call. Action items:
- kevin: prototype `preserve_signed_canonical` toggle + annotate injection middleware (canary route)
- mai: add integration test and record failing example to repro suite
- eli: update telemetry design for `x-client-id-raw` vs public header and write short doc on header annotation semantics

kevin: I'll push a small patch to the gateway branch today and wire a canary for `/uploads/*` routes — will ping when ready.

mai: sgtm :+1: keep infra-bot in the loop for canary rollout window.

sarah: Thanks team. Let's avoid changing auth service right now unless needed.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: gateway-edge-canary-3 -> 15% traffic -> 2026-02-03 18:00 UTC (ETA 30m).

eli: Also adding a note: update console route editor UX to expose `preserve_signed_canonical` (checkbox) with tooltip explaining signed URLs. Small UX task but crucial for customer self-serve.

sarah: Perfect. Closing the loop here — will follow up if additional fails come in.
